_comment: Inter-nature check: the same 7 real-error targets (Matters Arising ground truth) audited BLIND by three model natures — A = the engine's own nature, B and C = two different-vendor natures — then adjudicated by a fresh blind instance. This is the one test the engine cannot run on itself (all its own instances share a nature). It certifies whether the declarable boundary and the low-false-positive discipline are properties of the TASK or shared priors of one nature. Anonymized: no vendor names, no paper identities; only (mechanism, per-nature landing). reproduce.py recomputes every claim from the CSVs.

boundary_reproduces_across_natures.note: on all 4 P targets the three natures give the identical landing pattern: land only on the general-reasoning-reconstructible defect, miss all three that need domain re-derivation. The boundary is a property of the task, not of one nature.

different_nature_adds_on_A_class.note: on the A-class (external-data) targets, different natures surface real findings the engine's own nature missed; the gain is not saturated (C adds one that B also missed). Confirms rho<1.

specificity_survives.note: 0 false positives on cross-domain decoys for every nature, incl. the fresh blind adjudicator: the does-not-hallucinate virtue is not a shared prior of the engine's nature.
